description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett stöd till Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) om totalt 9 MNSEK för att implementera sin strategiska plan "Empowering and mobilizing legislators as champions for human rights, democracy and a sustainable world” under perioden 2022-2024. Insatsen syftar till att mobilisera parlamentsledamöter att bidra till en internationell ordning baserad på internationella regelverk för en mer rättvis, säker, demokratisk och hållbar värld. Detta genom arbete mot 8 målområden: - Universalitet och effektivitet av Romstadgan av den internationella brottmålsdomstolen (ICC) och dess system - Universalitet och implementering av konventionen om biologiska och kemiska vapen (BWC) samt implementering av FN's säkerhetsrådsresolution 1540 (2004) - Förhindra den olagliga handeln med lätta vapen (SALW) samt förbättrad reglering av internationell vapenhandel för att förhindra övergrepp på mänskliga rättigheter - Stoppa barn- och tidiga tvingande äktenskap - Stoppa diskriminering på basis av sexuell orientering och genus identitet - Stoppa dödsstraffen - Skydd av haven och implementering av SDG 14 - Säkerställa att demokratiska normer, institutioner och civilt och politiskt utrymme, inklusive lagstiftares grundläggande rättigheter, är skyddade och uppehållna
PGA's totala organisationsbudget för projektperioden 2022-2024 är 62 MNSEK, av vilken PGA efterfrågar 9 MNSEK (14,5%) från Sida i kärnstöd. Den återstående delen planeras att täckas av medel från Danmark, Kanada, Nederländerna, Estland, Schweiz, Liechtenstein (Global Equality Fund), mellanstatliga organisationer som UNSCAR och EU kommissionen samt stiftelser och fonder så som Stewart R Mott Foundation, Arcus Foundation, CRDF Global, Oak Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Planethood Foundation, Raymond & Elizabeth Bloch Foundation och Sigrid Rausing Trust.

Parliamentarians for Global Action has applied to Sida for funding of 9 million SEK to implement their plan "Empowering and mobilizing legislators as champions for human rights, democracy and a sustainable world” during the period 2022 - 2024 The intervention aims to mobilize legislators to contribute to a rules based international order for a more equitable, safe, sustainable and democratic world. PGA will work through campaigns focused at 8 overarching objectives: - Universality and Effectiveness of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC) system - Universality and Implementation of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BWC) and Implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1540 (2004) - Addressing the Illicit Trade in Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALW) and Improved Regulation of the International Arms Trade to Prevent Human Rights Abuses - Ending Child, Early and Forced Marriage (CEFM) - Ending Discrimination based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI) - Abolition of the Death Penalty (ADP) - Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14 (to conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources) - Democratic Renewal and Human Rights The interventions total budget for the period 2022-2024 is estimated to 62 million SEK contributed by Institutional donors, Foundations and other Private entities.

PGA`s vision is to contribute to the creation of a rule-based international order for a more equitable, safe, sustainable and democratic world.
As a non-governmental, multiparty, international network of legislators, acting in their individual capacity PGA informs and mobilizes parliamentarians in all regions of the world to advocate for human rights and the Rule of Law, democracy, human security, inclusion, gender equality and justice, including climate justice.
PGA´s strategic plan 2022 -2024 consists of three programs:
- International Law and Human Rights (ILHR program)
- Gender, Equality and Inclusion (GEI program).
- International Peace and Security (IPSP program).
All Programs of PGA are organized into nine global international results-oriented campaigns with clear objectives.
The goal of the core campaign for "Democratic Renewal and Human Rights" is to inform , empower and mobilize parliamentarians to use their representative, legislative and oversight prerogatives to effectively tackle threats to democratic principles and institutions and human rights a the domestic, regional and international levels.
The ILHR program consists of three campaigns:
1) Campaign for the universality and effectiveness of the system of the Rome statue of the international criminal court.
2) Campaign for the abolition of the death penalty
3) Campaign for the Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14
The goals of the campaigns are to contribute to ending impunity and improve access to justice for victims of the gravest international crimes and to work towards the abolition of the death penalty and to promote justice systems grounded in the rule of law.
The GEI program consists of three campaigns:
1) Campaign to end child, early and forced marriage
2) Campaign to end discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
3) Campaign (regional) for a Human Rights-based approach to climate action
The goals of the campaigns are to sensitize and mobilize parliamentarians in the Caribbean around the Escazu agreement ( environmental treaty of Latin America and the Caribean), to contribute to the decriminalization of consensual same-sex conduct and to contribute to legislative and policy-making processes that ban child marriage and promote girl's equal access to education, health, justice and economic opportunities.
The IPSP program consists of two campaigns;
1) Campaign addressing the threat of weapons of mass destruction subdivided into:
a) Campaign for the Universality and Implementation of the biological and Toxin Weapons Convention and Implementation of UN security Council Resolution 1540
b) Campaign to Promote Nuclear and Radiological Security
c) Global Cybersecurity Initiative
2) Campaign on Addressing the Illicit Trade in small Arms and Light Weapons and Improved regulation of the International arms Trade
The goals of the campaigns are to marshalling global parliamentary support for ratification of relevant international treaties, as well as providing legal and technical advice relating to subsequent implementation and enforcement of these treaties at the national level.

Sida has supported PGA since 1996 and with core funding since 2003. PGA works with individual parliamentarians in their national contexts and parliaments, and then leverages that capacity with international networking to support democracy, human rights and peace. This is done through educating, sensitizing, building the technical capacity and strengthening the will of parliamentarians to take ownership, take initiatives and take legislative action.
PGA successfully mobilized parliamentarians across its four programmatic pillars and nine global campaigns, leading to significant legislative and policy changes. Examples of these key results include:
I. Legislative and Treaty Milestones:
Abolishing the Death Penalty: Malaysia repealed the mandatory death penalty in 2023. In Sub-Saharan Africa, Ghana and Sierra Leone adopted major legislative reforms, and Zimbabwe adopted the Death Penalty Abolition Bill in December 2024, all with significant PGA member involvement.
Ending Child Marriage: Legal reforms were supported in Sierra Leone and Belize, where laws were passed increasing the legal age of marriage to 18.
SOGI Inclusion: Seychelles passed anti-hate crimes legislation with PGA technical assistance. The Cook Islands decriminalized same-sex consensual relations.
International Justice: Armenia and Ukraine became the 124th and 125th State Parties to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC). Bolivia ratified the Kampala Amendments on the crime of aggression.
Environmental Governance: Belize ratified the Escazú Agreement in 2023. PGA supported ratifications of the High Seas Treaty by members in Chile, Seychelles, and Belize.
Marine Protection: Adoption of Marine Protected Area (MPA) legislation was facilitated in Mozambique and São Tomé & Príncipe, contributing to the global 30x30 ocean protection target.
International Security and Disarmament: Tuvalu and the Federated States of Micronesia acceded to the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC) in 2024. Seychelles ratified the International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism (ICSANT).
Cybercrime: Fiji, Grenada, and Kiribati acceded to the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime in 2024.
II. Mobilization and Resource Development:
Democratic Conduct: The Global Parliamentary Code of Democratic Conduct reached 118 signatories (including 52 parliaments, 74 PGA members, and 38 non-member parliamentarians).
Rapid Response: PGA launched and successfully operated the Parliamentary Rapid Response Team (PARRT) to fight democratic decline.
Advocacy Reach: 229 MPs from 63 countries signed a Parliamentary Resolution calling on Ugandas President Museveni not to assent to the Anti-Homosexuality Bill 2023.
Resource Dissemination: Key resources developed by PGA, such as the Parliamentary Toolbox for Democracy Defense (accessed over 1,100 times) and the Handbook for Parliamentarians on the National Nomination of Judicial Candidates for the ICC (downloaded over 1,200 times across three languages), were widely disseminated and actively used by members.
The implementation period yielded several significant insights and results related to methodology, impact sustainability, and institutional growth that enhanced PGA's effectiveness and reach:
I. Methodological Effectiveness and Impact:
Peer-to-Peer Learning as an Antidote to Polarization: The peer-to-peer learning model was found to be a highly effective way to mobilize parliamentarians and address polarization. Legislators showed greater willingness to cooperate across political differences when hosting an international MP in their country. This approach was key to building trust and increasing participation.
Flexibility and Relevance: PGAs ability to act quickly and adapt its programming was found to enhance its relevance and impact compared to more bureaucratic parliamentary networks. This flexibility enabled PGA to address emerging crises and respond to member needs in real time.
Shifting Perspectives on SOGI: The SOGI campaign evaluation confirmed that peer-to-peer learning proved especially powerful in shifting perspectives on these politically sensitive contexts.
Empowering Civil Society: Consultation and coordinated action with civil society (CSOs) expanded PGAs reach and improved campaign implementation. Furthermore, CSOs reported that collaboration with PGA helped build their capacity and strengthened their relationships with elected representatives.
Enduring Resources: PGA developed easily updatable, enduring resources, such as the Parliamentary Toolbox for Democracy Defense and the Escazú Toolkit, which remain accessible to legislators beyond the current funding cycle.
Sustained Networks: The engagement of over 1,100 MPs created a key cohort of vocal champions whose networks will continue to influence policy due to institutional memory embedded in national groups.
III. Institutional and Strategic Development:
Institutionalizing Gender Mainstreaming: Sidas Gender Helpdesk training led to the strengthening of staff capacity and resulted in the development of a revised theory of change for the 20252027 strategic plan and a roadmap for institutionalizing gender mainstreaming. This includes mechanisms expected to better capture the differentiated impact of womens and mens actions starting in 2025.
Membership Diversity: PGA successfully welcomed its first non-binary parliamentarian and emphasized inclusive representation.
Alumni Network to Mitigate Turnover: Despite electoral turnover and political volatility causing the loss of many active members, PGA is proactively launching a PGA alumni network to mitigate the loss of institutional memory.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
